A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Clipped Density and Clipped Coverage research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching analyses relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original metric experiments on Gaussian and CIFAR-10 data, evaluations of generated images across four datasets, implementation timings, sensitivity analyses, and benchmark results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds clipping ablations, an outlier case study, a generated chest X-ray evaluation, and image-distortion experiments.

M1.justification: The individual-contribution clipping, median-radius clipping for Density, leave-one-out normalization, and theoretical Coverage calibration remain unchanged. Section 4 reorganizes and clarifies these procedures; the new appendix ablations evaluate intermediate variants without changing the proposed metrics.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds medical-image evaluation using a ChestX-ray8-trained Progressively Growing GAN. Appendix G adds distorted CIFAR-10 scenarios, including blurring, cropping, color changes, and elastic transformation. These substantially extend the represented domains and input conditions beyond the retained natural-image and Gaussian evaluations.

E2.justification: The metric comparators in Section 5 and the relocated benchmark tables are retained. Appendix G references FLD and FID findings from another study, but Figure 8 reports only Clipped Density, with previously evaluated generative models supplying reference scores; it does not newly evaluate FLD or FID.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce staged clipping controls, over-occurring sample proportions, and specified distortions such as hue 0.3 and center crop 28. For the existing CIFAR-10 mode-dropping test, v1 describes retaining 10% of real data per class, whereas v2 describes an unchanged real set. This revises the reported control without establishing a rerun; the shared metric parameters and embedding model remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E newly isolates the effects of radius clipping, individual-contribution clipping, and normalization across all four existing image datasets. Appendix D investigates which real CIFAR-10 samples inflate RESFLOW's Density, and Appendix G tests sensitivity to image distortions. These substantially strengthen component and failure-mechanism analysis beyond the retained stress tests and k-sensitivity study.

E5.justification: The reported ten CIFAR-10 splits, five Gaussian-translation splits, and ten toy-data repetitions are retained, as is the benchmark's hash-dependent seed explanation. The new analyses introduce no additional uncertainty-estimation method, significance test, or reported increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Tables 2–6 add ball-occupancy counts, over-occurring sample proportions, and intermediate clipping results beyond the previously plotted endpoints. Appendix F newly reports chest X-ray Clipped Density of 0.06 and Clipped Coverage of 0.03; Figure 8 adds distortion-dependent scores. The implementation table's numerical entries and relocated benchmark pass/fail entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: Lemma 1's beta-binomial expectation, its Appendix A proof, and Appendix B's computational derivations remain mathematically unchanged. Equation reordering and more explicit calibration-index wording clarify existing mathematics without introducing a new theorem or correction.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same two metrics and central claims of robustness, sensitivity, linear degradation, and interpretable absolute scores. The additional experiments support and apply these retained contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies embedding-model choice as unresolved, attributes RESFLOW's inflated Density to particular real outliers, and interprets the new chest X-ray scores as indicating insufficient fitness for use. These add qualifications and application-specific interpretations while retaining the central calibration interpretation and existing benchmark and memorization limitations.

D1.justification: v2 specifies FFHQ's 256×256 resolution, identifies the Medigan medical-model source, and documents distortion parameter choices. It replaces the named GitHub code link with an anonymous repository link. The existing nearest-neighbor implementation details, hardware description, and computation-time estimates are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the FLD reference and sources for progressive GANs, Medigan, the chest X-ray model, and ChestX-ray8. The Räisä benchmark gains prominence in the introduction and related work but was already discussed and evaluated in v1 Appendix I. The underlying research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Extensive prose editing accompanies substantial reorganization: Section 4 changes from grouping by desideratum to grouping by metric, Section 5 gains explicit subsections and named tests, and the appendices are reordered around the additions. The separate broader-impact section is removed.

P2.justification: v2 adds diagnostic and component-ablation tables, a four-image outlier gallery, and a distortion chart with example images. Retained plots receive color, legend, axis-label, and caption revisions, while figures and text are extensively repositioned within the changed document layout. Existing appendix plots are largely retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new component ablations and RESFLOW case study provide more direct support for the clipping mechanism than v1's aggregate comparisons, while distortion tests and clearer method organization improve evaluation and readability. These gains are tempered by Appendix F's strong medical fitness-for-purpose conclusion from two metric scores without clinical or downstream validation reported in the PDFs. Overall, the revision provides a limited net quality improvement.
